newsitem.title: USA: Atrix Leuprolide testing seen in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Atrix Leuprolide testing seen in 1998.

text.p: Atrix Laboratories Inc President and Chief Scientific Officer G. Lee Southard said on Thursday Atrix expects its Leuprolide drug to treat prostate cancer to be in Phase I clinical testing in 1998.
"We're at the mid to late stage pre-clinical," he told the Colorado Bio Investment Conference here.
"We're very optimistic that that's going to go forward," he said. The drug would be marketed by Gensia Inc on a global basis, he said.

Southard said later it is important for Atrix to expand into developing anti-cancer drugs because of their potential. The company has been involved in developing drugs to treat periodontal disease, which Southard called the "No. 1 chronic disease in the world."
Atrix plans to file for a new drug application (NDA) "within the next couple of months" for Atridox which would provide for a less invasive treatment of periodontal disease.
Atridox would stop the infection and inflammation around a tooth that is caused by plaque and, if untreated, leads to tooth loss.
Southard said Atridox is the only product aimed at avoiding the painful procedure of scaling and root planing.
